title: Majestic Victory
informationNeeded: A full-board image or FEN/PGN for the starting position and the later c8 rook/queen-promotion comparison. The current crop omits the upper ranks; include both kings and every piece.
reviewNotes: Accepted crops and the flagged montage omit the upper board and do not establish a complete legal position. No alternate saved uncropped video/frame was found locally. Captions describe a rook-underpromotion study but cannot supply the unseen squares.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players will accept a draw, but only a true genius would be able to find the incredible win that white has in this position. It seems like there's no way to make any progress because the black rook will always be able to sacrifice itself for the last pawn and at least secure a draw. But white has an incredible resource in this position. Of course, we start with C7, getting one step closer to our new queen. Now the king is defending C5 and the pawn is defending D8. So there is no way for the rook [music] to attack the pawn. But of course, the rook can give this check and force the king to move. If the king moves to B7, this is a massive mistake. This blunders a draw after rook to D7. The pawn is pinned to the king and inevitably black is going to sacrifice the rook for the pawn and draw the game just like this. And king to C5 would blunder another draw after rook to D1, skewering the king [music] from behind. And actually, if you get a new queen, we are actually going to lose the new queen and with it we are going [music] to lose the game like this. So the first very precise move that white needs to find is king to B5, relinquishing control of the pawn, but still defending all of these key squares that don't allow the rook to attack the pawn. But of course, the rook can give a check. So actually, we need to keep [music] going down and the rook has to keep checking us. We go down and the rook checks us. But now the situation has changed. The rook is bound to the limits of the chessboard, so we can go to C7 and the rook runs out of squares. It cannot create the skewer threat anymore. But do not celebrate too soon because black does have a last mysterious move with rook to D4. This sets up an incredible trap. If we now try to get a new queen, this is actually a massive blunder after the genius move rook to C4, sacrificing the rook completely to attack the king and queen at the same time. But of course, once we take this rook, the game is going to end with a stalemate and a draw. The king is not in check, but it doesn't have any legal moves. So believe it or not, the only [music] way for white to win in this position is to promote to a rook. Now of course, the stalemating trap doesn't work anymore and we [music] are creating a checkmate threat with the king and rook. And some of you might think, well, this doesn't make any sense as the board is saying the rook can simply cover the checkmate threat and now this is a draw. We both have one rook left. But you would be mistaken. After king to B3, we are attacking [music] the rook and creating a new checkmate threat that cannot be stopped in any way, which means that black has no other choice but to give us the rook. And this is just going to be a textbook win for white. [music] If you want a majestic board like this one, use code Pietro 10 for a discount. The link is in my bio.
